title: Prevent sexual acquisition of HIV with twice-yearly injections

concept.text: Provide effective HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis with six-monthly maintenance injections. Lenacapavir achieved this dosing interval, with HIV testing and management of resistance risk remaining essential. Proposed completion test: FDA approval for PrEP in HIV-negative adults and adolescents weighing at least 35 kg, supported by phase 3 HIV-incidence endpoints and a maintenance injection interval of six months. Test set by: FDA; PURPOSE trial protocols supplied the incidence comparisons accepted in the approval. Reported achieved: FDA approved lenacapavir (Yeztugo) for PrEP on 18 June 2025. Sources given: [FDA original Yeztugo prescribing information](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/220020s000lbl.pdf) ; [Current Yeztugo label and approval record](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=1c241af1-ce62-4b0a-9eb7-f6b626174f01).

page.title: Twice-yearly injectable HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis
page.definition: Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) means taking medicine before potential exposure to reduce the risk of infection. Lenacapavir is the first regimen with maintenance injections every six months to reduce the risk of sexually acquired HIV-1 in people without HIV. The earlier injectable option, cabotegravir, requires maintenance injections every two months.

goal.need: An estimated 1.2 million people acquired HIV worldwide in 2025. Daily oral PrEP is effective when taken as prescribed, yet about half of US users stop within 6–12 months. For people who find a daily pill hard to take or keep private, twice-yearly PrEP provides protection between injections and requires fewer injection visits than cabotegravir. Continued protection depends on access to scheduled doses and HIV testing.

statements.quote: LEN’s twice-yearly dosing offers a significant advantage for people who face challenges with adhering to daily oral PrEP
the CDC PrEP Guidelines Work Group strongly recommends lenacapavir injections as an HIV PrEP option

completion.title: FDA approves HIV-1 pre-exposure prophylaxis given by injection every six months.
completion.criterion: FDA approves a medicine for pre-exposure prophylaxis to reduce the risk of sexually acquired HIV-1, with a labeled maintenance schedule of one injection visit every six months after initiation.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, approval letter for Yeztugo injection (NDA 220018) and prescribing information, sections 1 and 2.3.
completion.threshold_quote: 6-months (26 weeks) from the date of the last injection +/-2 weeks.
completion.basis: FDA approved Yeztugo injection on 18 June 2025 for adults and adolescents weighing at least 35 kg who are at risk of sexually acquired HIV-1. After initiation, each 927 mg dose consists of two subcutaneous injections at one visit, scheduled 26 weeks after the preceding dose with a two-week window on either side. The separate tablet approval is NDA 220020.

milestones.set_by: The GS-CA1 study investigators, including Gilead Sciences and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, in the published macaque-study methods. This test concerns a lenacapavir analogue.

milestones.title: Lenacapavir’s HIV-1 incidence ratio to background is <0.5 with an upper 95% confidence limit <0.8.
milestones.criterion: In each of PURPOSE 1 and PURPOSE 2, perform the planned interim analysis when 50% of randomized participants have completed at least 52 weeks of follow-up or discontinued. Divide HIV-1 incidence on twice-yearly lenacapavir by estimated background incidence without PrEP. FDA’s agreed interim success criterion is a point estimate <0.5 and an upper 95% confidence limit <0.8, with one-sided α = 0.0026.
milestones.set_by: FDA Division of Antivirals, agreed PURPOSE 1 and PURPOSE 2 interim-analysis success criteria reproduced in section 8 of its Breakthrough Therapy Designation review.
milestones.threshold_quote: (bHIV) < 0.8 with the point estimate being < 0.5 (1-sided alpha of 0.0026).

milestones.title: Lenacapavir shows lower HIV-1 incidence than daily oral PrEP at one-sided α = 0.0026.
milestones.criterion: At the planned interim analysis of each PURPOSE trial, after the background-incidence test succeeds, demonstrate superiority of twice-yearly lenacapavir over daily oral emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate. Compare HIV-1 incidence rates using their ratio, with a one-sided significance level of 0.0026.
milestones.set_by: FDA Division of Antivirals, agreed key secondary interim-analysis criteria; the sequential tests and results appear in section 14 of the original Yeztugo prescribing information.
milestones.threshold_quote: superiority of LEN over F/TDF using the rate ratio metrics (1-sided alpha of 0.0026).

milestones.title: A candidate’s concentrations for 50% and 90% inhibition of HIV-1 replication are measured in culture.
milestones.criterion: Measure the concentrations of the candidate that inhibit HIV-1 replication by 50% and 90% in a quantitative cell-culture assay. These measurements characterize antiviral potency before human testing.
milestones.set_by: FDA, nonclinical virology guidance for HIV-1 drugs, incorporated by reference in section II.A of its 2019 systemic PrEP guidance.
milestones.threshold_quote: The effective concentration (EC) at which virus replication is inhibited by 50 and 90 percent

In the healthy-volunteer phase 1 study (n = 40), lenacapavir’s median apparent terminal half-life was about 38 days.

results.finding: PURPOSE 2 lenacapavir (n=2179) versus estimated background (n=4634) had an HIV incidence rate ratio of 0.04.
results.detail: The interim trigger was based on 3000 planned participants. Actual randomization totaled 3292, and the paper does not establish that half of those participants had completed at least 52 weeks or discontinued at the interim analysis.

results.finding: Lenacapavir showed no effects on rat fertility at 8 times human systemic exposure. The label gives no animal count.

when lenacapavir was administered to rats at systemic exposures (AUC) 8 times the

results.finding: Subcutaneous lenacapavir reached peak concentration after 77–84 days in humans. The label gives no sample size for this estimate.
results.detail: The pharmacokinetic result appears in Table 8.

results.finding: Lenacapavir beat background HIV-1 incidence at interim analysis in both PURPOSE trials (lenacapavir n=2,134 and n=2,179).

results.finding: FDA approved Yeztugo (lenacapavir) for HIV-1 PrEP with one maintenance injection visit every 6 months.
results.detail: Each maintenance visit includes two subcutaneous injections that together deliver the full dose.

definition = "Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) means taking medicine before potential exposure to reduce the risk of infection. Lenacapavir is the first regimen with maintenance injections every six months to reduce the risk of sexually acquired HIV-1 in people without HIV. The earlier injectable option, cabotegravir, requires maintenance injections every two months.". Reason: The definition omits the first medicine to meet it and the dosing interval of the earlier injectable option.

goal.need = "An estimated 1.2 million people acquired HIV worldwide in 2025. Daily oral PrEP is effective when taken as prescribed, yet about half of US users stop within 6\u201312 months. For people who find a daily pill hard to take or keep private, twice-yearly PrEP provides protection between injections and requires fewer injection visits than cabotegravir. Continued protection depends on access to scheduled doses and HIV testing.". Reason: The newer global estimate and the practical differences between daily pills, two-monthly injections and six-monthly injections explain who benefits and what continued protection requires.

add statement by World Health Organization, 2025: "WHO recommends offering the six-monthly injectable lenacapavir (LEN) as an additional HIV prevention option.". Reason: WHO’s formal 2025 recommendation adds a decision that its 2024 statement about interim results could only anticipate.

add statement by National Institute for Health and Care Excellence, 2026: "the cost-effectiveness estimates are above the range that NICE considers an acceptable use of NHS resources". Reason: The September 2026 draft appraisal records a health technology assessment body’s reservation about NHS funding at the cost assessed.
